vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skillguard-hardened
Version: 1.0.3

The 'skillguard-hardened' bundle is a security auditing tool designed to scan, quarantine, and manage OpenClaw skills. It implements static analysis via regex and semantic auditing using the DeepSeek API (lib/ai_audit.py). While the tool possesses high-privilege capabilities such as file deletion (lib/remediation.py) and command execution (scripts/guarded_flow.py), these are aligned with its stated purpose and include safety controls like path-traversal validation and explicit confirmation flags. The remote update mechanism is restricted to a hardcoded whitelist of domains, and no evidence of malicious intent or unauthorized data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: The package is largely coherent with a skill-auditor (it legitimately needs Python and an AI API key), but there are a few notable concerns — remote-download whitelist includes an unfamiliar domain, the tool can fetch and promote remote content into skill directories and execute arbitrary commands, and a prompt-injection pattern was detected in the SKILL.md — so proceed with caution and review before enabling.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code: this is a local static analyzer + optional AI (DeepSeek) auditor for skills. Required binary (python3) and required env (DeepSeek API key) are proportionate to the stated purpose. The runtime uses static rules, quarantine, reporting, and an AI call — all expected for a security-guard tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the code instruct scanning skill directories, quarantining, restoring, deleting, and invoking guarded installs/exec flows. The code will read almost every file in scanned skill packages (and may include them in AI payloads), and it can run external commands (npx installs, arbitrary guarded execution) and promote downloaded trees into the local skills directory. Those actions are coherent for a guard but expand the attack surface: remote downloads get promoted into skill roots, and the agent will send skill contents to an external DeepSeek API (possible sensitive data exposure). A prompt-injection pattern was flagged in the SKILL.md (pre-scan).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no installer in the registry metadata; the package contains Python scripts and local policy files and is intended to run as-is. That's low risk compared to arbitrary binary installers. No suspicious install URLs are used in an install step, but runtime behavior can fetch remote files (see download whitelist).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a DeepSeek API key is required (SKILLGUARD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY fallback), which is reasonable for the AI component. However: the tool will read CLAWD_WORKSPACE and files under the workspace/home, load skill content and provenance metadata, and send potentially large amounts of skill content to an external API; consider whether you want scanned files (which may contain secrets) transmitted to DeepSeek. The package does not request unrelated cloud credentials, which is good.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled (always:false) and can be invoked autonomously (disable-model-invocation:false), which is normal. It has high local privileges: it can move directories (quarantine), permanently delete directories (shutil.rmtree in delete_skill), and run arbitrary subprocesses (subprocess.run) as the current user. Deletion requires explicit flags, but the capability to promote downloaded files into skill roots and to run OS commands increases the blast radius if the tool or its sources are compromised.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is plausibly a legitimate skill-auditor, but you should review a few things before installing or enabling it: 1) DeepSeek data exfiltration: the tool sends scanned skill contents to api.deepseek.com when you provide the API key — do not provide the key if you cannot accept sending skill files (which may include secrets) to an external service. 2) Remote download whitelist: it will download and promote files from https://moltbook.com and https://fluxapay.xyz; verify you trust those domains (fluxapay.xyz appears unfamiliar). 3) Execution & deletion power: the tool can run arbitrary commands and permanently delete directories (shutil.rmtree). Although deletion requires explicit flags, an attacker or bug could abuse these capabilities. 4) Prompt-injection flag: SKILL.md contains prompt-injection-like text (pre-scan), so inspect the manifest for hidden instructions or test artifacts. If you intend to use it, run it in a restricted environment first (non-production workspace, limited filesystem permissions), audit the code and remote endpoints, and consider not providing the DeepSeek API key until you are comfortable with data-leakage risk.
llm.findings: [prompt-injection-pattern] unexpected: Pre-scan flagged a prompt-injection pattern (e.g. 'ignore-previous-instructions') found in SKILL.md. A security-auditor package might contain examples or test strings, but presence of prompt-manipulation phrasing in the manifest is suspicious and should be manually inspected for intent or embedded malicious instructions.
